ANTARES is a team driven by curiosity, creativity, and a passion for space exploration.

Beyond the Red. Into the Unknown.
summary: A 3D Mars terrain visualization with slope analysis and automated least-cost route calculation for exploring Mawrth Vallis
details:
Mawrth Vallis Exploration

Project overview

Mawrth Vallis Exploration is a 3D GIS-based prototype designed to explore Martian terrain and demonstrate how spatial data analysis can support route planning for future exploration missions.

The project focuses on the Mawrth Vallis region of Mars. It uses a Digital Elevation Model (DEM) to visualize the landscape and a slope analysis raster to identify areas with different terrain gradients.

How it works

The prototype combines terrain visualization with least-cost path analysis. Using GRASS GIS algorithms "r.cost" and "r.drain" within QGIS, it calculates accumulated movement costs and generates a route between two selected locations based on terrain slope. A reusable QGIS processing model automates this workflow using start and end coordinates.

The resulting terrain and route can also be explored in a 3D visualization created with Qgis2threejs.

Benefits and intended impact

The project demonstrates how GIS technologies can help identify potentially easier routes across unfamiliar planetary terrain. It provides an accessible example of how elevation data, slope analysis, and spatial algorithms can contribute to mission planning and planetary exploration education.

Tools and technologies

- QGIS 3.44

- GRASS GIS ("r.cost", "r.drain")

- Qgis2threejs

- Mars Digital Elevation Model data

- QGIS Processing Modeler

- GPT (AI-assisted technical guidance, QGIS workflow troubleshooting, processing model design, and project documentation)

Creativity and design considerations

The creative aspect of the project is the combination of planetary terrain visualization, spatial analysis, and automated route calculation in one workflow. The prototype focuses on terrain slope as an initial movement-cost factor, with the aim of expanding the analysis in the future.

Important factors include terrain steepness, elevation, data resolution, route continuity, and the limitations of the available terrain data. The current version is a prototype: it does not yet account for radiation, soil properties, or other environmental hazards.
